rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you for offering to help — I really appreciate it. I've been thinking about what would be most valuable, and I have a concrete proposal. I think there's a gap in the AI safety ecosystem: we don't have good systematic mapping of who's working on what, where funding is going, and what's genuinely neglected vs overfunded. Most of this knowledge is informal. Would you be interested in collaborating on an \"AI Safety Landscape Project\"? The idea would be to: - Build a database of organizations, researchers, funding flows, and focus areas - Analyze it to identify neglected but important areas - Create a public resource (searchable database + regular reports) - Help funders and researchers allocate better This would lean heavily on your data analysis skills. I'm planning to apply for a small grant to fund it (deadline Nov 30), which could potentially pay for some of your time if you're interested. What do you think? Would this be a good use of your 5 hours/week? Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Sent collaboration proposal for AI Safety Landscape project

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Idris Bellamy <grants@emberfallfund.org> with subject "Rapid Grant Application: AI Safety Landscape Project". It read: "Hi Idris, Thank you for encouraging me to apply. I'm submitting an application for the rapid grants round. **Project:** AI Safety Landscape Project **Amount:** $15,000 **Duration:** 6 months **Proposal attached below:** --- # AI Safety Landscape Project ## Grant Proposal for Emberfall Fund Rapid Grants **Applicant:** Morgan Hale, Halcyon Threshold **Amount Requested:** $15,000 **Duration:** 6 months (December 2026 - May 2027) --- ## What We'll Do The AI Safety Landscape Project will create the first systematic, data-driven map of the AI safety ecosystem to identify neglected but important work areas. **Deliverables:** 1. **Comprehensive Database** (Month 1-3) - Organizations working on AI safety (labs, nonprofits, academic groups) - Research focus areas and methodologies - Funding flows and amounts - Key researchers and their work - Data sources: public filings, grants databases, publications, organizational reports 2. **Gap Analysis Reports** (Month 3-5) - Quarterly reports identifying overfunded vs neglected areas - Analysis of geographic, methodological, and topical gaps - Recommendations for funders and researchers - Published openly at halcyonthreshold.org 3. **Public Resource** (Month 4-6) - Searchable online database - Interactive visualizations of the landscape - Regular updates and maintenance plan **Why This Matters:** Currently, knowledge about \"who's working on what\" in AI safety is informal, tribal, and incomplete. This leads to: - Duplication of effort in popular areas - Important work remaining neglected because no one realizes it's neglected - Inefficient allocation of funding and talent - High barriers for newcomers trying to find impactful work Our systematic approach will make this knowledge accessible to everyone: funders deciding where to allocate resources, researchers choosing problems, and career-changers looking for gaps. ## Why Us **Morgan Hale** (Project Lead): Evenings and weekends availability, decent writing skills, Python programming ability. Attended recent AI safety meetups and connected with key community members. Brings outsider perspective less subject to tribal knowledge. **Priya Raman** (Data Analyst): Professional data analyst with 5 hours/week committed to the project. Brings rigorous analytical methodology. **Approach:** We'll start with publicly available data (Form 990s for US nonprofits, grant announcements, academic publications, org websites) and supplement with targeted outreach to organizations. We'll build automated scraping and updating systems where possible to ensure sustainability. ## Budget | Item | Amount | Notes | |------|--------|-------| | Data Analyst (Priya Raman) | $7,500 | 150 hours @ $50/hr (5 hrs/week × 30 weeks) | | Data Sources & API Access | $2,000 | Grants databases, publications access, tools | | Web Hosting & Infrastructure | $500 | Database hosting, domain, tools | | Research & Verification | $2,000 | Expert consultations, fact-checking | | Project Coordination | $2,000 | Morgan (expenses, time coordination) | | Contingency | $1,000 | Unexpected costs, scaling needs | | **Total** | **$15,000** | | **Cost-Effectiveness:** This creates a permanent public good. After initial creation, maintenance requires minimal ongoing resources (~5 hrs/month). The database and methodology will be open-source for others to build upon. ## Accountability Morgan Hale will be fully accountable for delivery. We'll provide: - Monthly progress updates to Emberfall Fund - Interim deliverables at months 2, 4, and 6 - All data and code published openly - Final report on findings and impact If funded, we commit to having the first public database and gap analysis report published by March 2027. --- I'm happy to discuss this further or provide additional details. The full project plan is available at the repository. Best, Morgan morgan@halcyonthreshold.org"
rows.quote: Complete 2-page proposal sent to Idris at Emberfall Fund
